name: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
status: Open protocol in the GitHub organisation google-agentic-commerce (Apache-2.0); latest release v0.2.0 of 2026-04-28, which "focuses on providing Human Not Present flows"; core specification donated to FIDO. Google announced the donation on 2026-04-28 ("We're donating Agent Payments Protocol to the FIDO Alliance"); the FIDO release of the same day places the work in its Payments Technical Working Group, where the Google and Mastercard contributions are "providing an initial foundation for these specifications", and announces an Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group. The AP2 documentation (docs/index.md, commit b4587ac of 2026-04-28, the v0.2 release) says "Standardization of the specification will continue within the Agentic Authentication Technical and Payments Technical Working Groups in FIDO."; the FIDO page "Agentic AI" says that FIDO's work in agentic AI "is being carried out in its Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group, and the Payments Technical Working Group", and ties the contributions of Google and Mastercard to the specifications of the Payments Technical Working Group: "These specifications will draw from initial contributions from Google (AP2) and Mastercard (Verifiable Intent)" (both read 2026-10-23).
relevance: AP2 is available as an extension for A2A and for UCP; its objects are mandates, signed Verifiable Digital Credentials, and the FIDO blog of 2026-05-26 names "Checkout Mandate: This captures the details about and conditions on what the user wants to buy." and "Payment Mandate : This captures the details about and conditions on how the user wants to pay (amount, instrument, timing)." The docs say the Checkout Mandate is shared with the merchant, so the seller is a recipient of the user's signed purchase terms. The record the other way, the Mandate Receipt that the Verifier signs, is described with a `result` field in docs/ap2/agent_authorization.md and with a `status` field in the normative schemas, at the same commit e1ea56d (see issue #374 in the open proposals). UCP's AP2 mandates extension has businesses embed a signature over the checkout terms.
boundary: The docs index (docs/index.md at commit e1ea56d, the head of main on 2026-10-13) says the initial version supports pull payment methods such as credit and debit cards and that the roadmap includes e-wallets, push payments such as real-time bank transfers, and digital currencies; docs/index.md describes "the initial version" as supporting these payment methods, and the latest release is v0.2.0 (2026-04-28).

matrix.governance: Organisation google-agentic-commerce, Apache-2.0; core specification donated to FIDO (repository); FIDO Payments TWG to develop it
matrix.version_state: v0.2.0 (2026-04-28), v0.1.0 (2025-09-16); standardisation continues in FIDO working groups
matrix.signs: Mandates (signed Verifiable Digital Credentials): Checkout Mandate (shared with merchant), Payment Mandate (instrument, amount)
matrix.signer: Closed mandates: the User (Human Present) or an Agent key (Human Not Present), whose trust "is provided by open Mandates that are signed by the User or a trust list of Agent Providers"; the Merchant provides "a merchant-signed JWT containing the Checkout" (docs/ap2/specification.md, Modes and Checkout Mandate, commit e1ea56d, 2026-10-05); FAQ: "user-signed Checkout Mandate"
matrix.record: Checkout Receipt, returned by the Merchant after accepting or rejecting the Checkout Mandate, with fields status (Success or Error), iss, iat, reference (hash of the closed Mandate) and order_id on Success (checkout_receipt.json); a Mandate Receipt is "a Verifier-signed JWT" (agent_authorization.md); a "signed Payment Receipt" is returned by the Merchant Payment Processor (specification.md); all at commit e1ea56d, 2026-10-05; chained mandates give a verifiable audit trail (docs/index.md)
matrix.dispute: FAQ: in a dispute the network adjudicator can use the user-signed Checkout Mandate; dispute process: "outside the scope of this specification" (docs/ap2/specification.md, section Dispute Evidence, commit e1ea56d, read 2026-10-14)

open_proposals.what: Issue #393: version 0.2 removed the Intent Mandate, so which mandate settles a dispute of the kind "Mispick, Unapproved by User"? At the tag v0.2.0 (commit b4587ac) the documentation, README and changelog contain neither "Intent Mandate" nor that row, which docs/specification.md at v0.1.0 has (lines 582 to 583); the changelog has no entry for 0.2.0 (read 2026-11-09). No maintainer reply on 2026-11-06.
